extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and researchers interested in participating in or proposing AIM workshops
extracted.subtask_description: Information for potential participants and proposers about American Institute of Mathematics (AIM) focused workshops, their distinguishing features, and how to apply or propose a workshop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop emphasis on a specific mathematical goal
rubrics_metrics.description: AIM focused workshops are distinguished by their emphasis on a specific mathematical goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of such goals include making progress on a significant unsolved problem, understanding the proof of an important new result, or examining the convergence of two distinct areas of mathematics. (Original wording: "AIM focused workshops are distinguished by their emphasis on a specific mathematical goal, such as making progress on a significant unsolved problem, understanding the proof of an important new result, or examining the convergence of two distinct areas of mathematics.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow application instructions listed per workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply to be a participant in a workshop follow the instructions in the list of upcoming workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific application instructions provided on each upcoming workshop listing. Workshops marked with an asterisk (*) are still open for applications. (Original wording: "To apply to be a participant in a workshop follow the instructions in the list of upcoming workshops. Those marked with an asterisk (*) are still open.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to propose a workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a process for proposing a workshop to AIM (link: 'Proposing a Workshop').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page directs users to a separate resource or page for information on proposing a workshop; no detailed proposal criteria are present on this specific page.
